designs.notes: Simulation only (xsim 2026.1, UVM 1.2; Icarus is not used by this bench). One recorded regression (results/176_seq_poison/summary.json) and one mutation record (results/170_itch_uvm/mutation_seed*.json). No board, no real feed, every message synthetic.

requirements.text: Each order frame with a good FCS equals the reference frame byte for byte (Ethernet, IPv4, TCP headers, SoupBinTCP 3.00 length and type, OUCH 5.0 Enter Order fields, ClOrdID, appendage), the orders come in order with UserRefNum rising by one per accepted candidate, and a frame with a wrong FCS is never an order.
requirements.title: Every order that leaves with a good frame check sequence is byte exact

requirements.text: For every packet the packet, message, gap, missing, duplicate, overlap, session, heartbeat, end-of-session, short, truncated and bad-length counters and the gap, session-lock and end-of-session flags equal the reference model's at every checkpoint, with 1, 3 and 6 messages a packet and at every frame alignment.
requirements.title: MoldUDP64 sessions, sequence gaps, duplicates, overlaps, heartbeats and broken packets are counted and delivered as the reference says

requirements.text: Message-type counters, malformed and skipped messages, unwatched locates, missing/duplicate/overflowing orders, ladder overflow and over-execution counters, the candidate count and the per-instrument inexact flags equal the reference model's, including the edge cases of an empty book, a full ladder, a table-index collision and a replace.
requirements.title: The ITCH decoder and the book keep the counters, the inexact flags and the candidates the reference model computes

requirements.text: Not armed, kill switch, untrusted or gap-halted, inexact book, quantity, position limit per instrument, price band and missing bid refuse a candidate exactly as the reference does; the position and the order number advance only for an accepted candidate.
requirements.title: Every risk refusal is the first failing check, counted once, and no order starts on a refused candidate

requirements.text: Destination MAC (unicast or the group's multicast address), EtherType, IPv4 version and header length, fragments, protocol, destination address and port, UDP length against the IP length, and the IPv4 header checksum; EN = 0 drops everything.
requirements.title: Frames are forwarded or dropped by the first failing header check, and each drop is counted

requirements.text: With STRICT set (the default, owner decision 31) no order leaves with a good FCS when the frame that carried its message has a bad FCS, or when that frame's verdict is not yet known at the order's last word; such an order leaves with a wrong FCS. Cut-through is a documented option with a measured window.
requirements.title: Under STRICT an order is never sent on an unverified or bad frame

requirements.text: The TCP sequence number of an order is the loaded number plus 59 for every segment that left with a good FCS; a frame poisoned (wrong FCS) by the multiplexer, because its trigger frame was bad or unverified, does not advance it.
requirements.title: A poisoned order frame consumes no TCP sequence number

requirements.text: Every bin of the bench's coverage plan (message types, messages a packet, Mold events, header drops, book edge cases, risk refusals, order outcomes, bad-FCS crosses, frame alignments, backpressure) is hit by the recorded regression.
requirements.title: The bench's functional coverage plan is closed

requirements.text: A blind mutation sweep (mutants made from the RTL text and a seed only, equivalent mutants decided by a formal miter) scores at least 90 % even if every undecided mutant counted as a survivor.
requirements.title: The bench kills at least 90 % of blind mutants of the path (worst case, over at least 30)

designs.notes: Simulation (cocotb on Icarus Verilog 12, one recorded pytest run) and out-of-context Vivado 2026.1 results only. No board run, no MAC of the 96 design in the simulation, no real TCP peer, no real exchange; every order is synthetic. Requirements that need those are hooks and show as not run.

requirements.text: For any connection state and order, the block sends 15 words (113 bytes without the frame check sequence) whose bytes equal the Python reference, with sequence number, acknowledgement number, window and IP identification captured at the go edge, the SoupBinTCP Unsequenced Data packet of brief 110 as payload, no TCP options and the PSH and ACK flags, including sequence numbers at the 32-bit wrap.
requirements.title: Each order leaves as one complete 113-byte Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP frame, byte exact against the reference

requirements.text: The IPv4 header checksum and the TCP checksum of every segment sent equal the reference's, which is itself checked against outside vectors (RFC 1071, a published IPv4 header), including carries in the fold, sums that wrap, a TCP checksum that comes out 0 and a segment whose headers sum to all ones. This is checked by simulation of chosen and random cases; the all-inputs statements are B119-F-CKSUM-IP, -TCP and -MODEL.
requirements.title: Both checksums on the wire are the RFC 1071 checksums, at the corner cases

requirements.text: One record (rec_v, rec_seq, rec_len, rec_id, rec_pay) for each unpoisoned segment in the clock of its last word, and none for a poisoned one, so software can retransmit from the records; a segment dropped on the wire is retransmitted by software with the same bytes.
requirements.title: Every segment that left is handed back to software, and none that was poisoned

requirements.text: Handshake, SoupBinTCP login, orders, acknowledgements, a dropped segment, heartbeats, a small window and a rejected login all behave as the software side documents, with the exchange seeing every order exactly once and in order.
requirements.title: A Python TCP owner and a software OUCH exchange run a whole session through the block

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall over tcp_fast.sv and the frame builder inside it reports no warnings, with the waivers in lint/lint_waivers.vlt.
requirements.title: The RTL lints clean

requirements.text: With tcp_fast in place of ouch_enter, brief 110's path against brief 110's reference model sends the same orders, with the same payload bytes, valid checksums and gapless sequence numbers; speculative orders that the risk logic refuses leave poisoned.
requirements.title: The block replaces the order port of brief 110 and works behind its risk logic

requirements.text: Writes to static fields invalidate the template and are ignored and counted while a segment is in flight; live fields are accepted at any time and restart the staleness age; reads show the registers before the next edge; unmapped addresses read 0; the 14 counters count what the datasheet says and clear on CLR_CNT.
requirements.title: The register bus and counters behave as the datasheet states

requirements.text: An abort at any of edges 1 to 14 ends the frame with o_poison, leaves SND_NXT and IP_ID as before and produces no record; an abort at edge 0 cancels the go; a speculative segment with no verdict by edge 14 is poisoned; an abort wins over a commit; an abort after the frame left is late, counted and ignored.
requirements.title: An aborted or unverdicted segment is poisoned and consumes no sequence space

requirements.text: Checked in the order busy, not armed, template not valid or state stale, window closed, MSS below 59, an order is refused with the matching code and counter, nothing leaves and no state changes; a window of exactly 59 bytes admits one segment and one byte less admits none.
requirements.title: The block refuses to send when it is not armed, stale, window-closed, too small or busy

requirements.text: Hardware and software share one sequence space. After a heartbeat takes it and gives it back, after an abort, after a refusal and after a retransmission, the peer's received stream has no gap and no duplicate, and nothing is sent by software while the block is armed and idle.
requirements.title: The peer sees no gap and no duplicate in the sequence space

requirements.text: The block sums the payload words ouch_enter actually emits and compares the total with the early one the checksum used; a difference (for example a configuration change in flight) poisons the segment and counts sumerr, so a wrong checksum is never sent as valid.
requirements.title: A segment whose payload disagrees with the checksum that was sent is poisoned

requirements.text: Every one of the seeded faults of verif/mutants.yaml that builds fails the bench (mutation score 100 percent, 73 of 73). The set is the agent's own; whether it is wide enough is the human's check.
requirements.title: A seeded fault anywhere in the checksum, segment, verdict, refusal or register logic is caught

requirements.title: The 96 design's MAC accepts the block's words every clock and corrupts the frame check sequence on o_poison

requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.
requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs

requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. designs.notes: Variants. Unless a requirement says otherwise, "the default build" is RATE_MATCH = 0 (the board-proven 97C receive path) and "the rate-matched build" is rm_gp (RATE_MATCH = 1, RM_OWN = 1). Board evidence is one KR260 on a short optical loopback; nothing has run against a network card. Briefs 112 (UVM bench), 115 (formal proofs of the rate matcher) and 123 (pyuvm bench) are merged and their tests are in the recorded run; the bound SVA checkers in simulation and the coverage run have no evidence and are shown as not run.

requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.
requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model

requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.
requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions

requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.
requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors

requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.
requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart

requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.
requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path

requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.
requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame

requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)
requirements.text: For any constant receive clock offset from -300 to +300 ppm relative to the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. IEEE 802.3 allows +-100 ppm at each end, so two compliant ends differ by at most 200 ppm; +-300 ppm gives margin. A loopback has no offset, so a board test needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset

requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.
requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card

requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.
requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned

requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.
requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails

requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.
requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed

requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.
requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions

requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.
requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing

requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.
requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly

requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.
requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents

requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.
requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does

requirements.text: A burst at line rate loses no frame. Nothing has been measured; the line and payload rates stand on configuration and gearbox arithmetic only.
requirements.title: Line-rate throughput without loss

requirements.text: Build dbg_xvc (the eyescan build plus a PS-AXI Debug Bridge and one ILA) closes timing and report_cdc, adds no cell to and removes no cell from the core's hierarchy except the read-only taps, and, on the board, Vivado finds and captures from the ILA over XVC while Linux keeps running. Never part of a build whose latency is measured.
requirements.title: A debug build reaches an ILA over the network and leaves the trading path alone

requirements.text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.
requirements.title: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width

requirements.text: For every width and value, the decoder of the pointer crossing returns the count the encoder was given; and a sampled code that is the old or the new code decodes to the old or the new count.
requirements.title: Gray decoding inverts gray encoding, at every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function adder (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/adder/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a bit-serial chain of full adders) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (ripple: 0; carry_select: 0; pipelined: STAGES), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/adder/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.source: arith/adder/rtl/adder_carry_select.sv (g_first and g_sel blocks, two blocks)
requirements.text: A carry-select adder (a low block, and a high block computed for carry in 0 and 1 and selected by the low block's carry out) returns the same sum and carry out as plain addition, for every block widths m and k and every pair of operands. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Carry-select composition adds, for every width

requirements.text: For every width n, a + ~b + ~bin on n bits equals a - b - bin modulo 2^n, and its carry out is 1 exactly when there is no borrow: the identity every variant's subtract path rests on. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Subtraction is addition of the complements, for every width

Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. requirements.text: arith/atan2_mag/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a floating-point CORDIC and the maths library's atan2 and hypot) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (10 exhaustive points, 7 random ones, across 2 variants), each variant's outputs equal its own model's (model.py, selected by variant) in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, table break points and random inputs at the large ones. The variants round differently and are not bit-identical to each other; the model of each is the bit-exact definition of that variant, and its distance from the exact function is the accuracy requirement.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against its own model

requirements.text: Each of the 3 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A point not listed has no stated bound.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is within the stated bound, at every listed point

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (cordic: NIT + 2; cordic_g2: -(-NIT // GRP) + 2), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is bounded for all inputs, by proof, at a small input width

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/atan2_mag/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function exp2 (brief 139d). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/exp2/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (exact rational (Fraction) evaluations of the interpolation and Horner formulas, a floating-point hyperbolic CORDIC, and the maths library's 2**x) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 12 random ones, across 4 variants), each variant's outputs equal its own model's (model.py, selected by variant) in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, table break points and random inputs at the large ones. The variants round differently and are not bit-identical to each other; the model of each is the bit-exact definition of that variant, and its distance from the exact function is the accuracy requirement.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against its own model

requirements.text: Each of the 12 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A point not listed has no stated bound.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is within the stated bound, at every listed point

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (table: REG; lerp: 2; poly2: 3; cordic: NIT + 1), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is bounded for all inputs, by proof, at a small input width

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/exp2/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). requirements.source: arith/exp2/rtl/exp2_lerp.sv (the product, sum and shift lines of the interpolation)
requirements.text: In a rising segment with break-point value c0 and slope s, the interpolated value (c0 * 2^D + s * d) / 2^D lies between c0 and c0 + s for every position d below 2^D and every D: the table variant cannot overshoot its segment. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation stays between the segment's end values, for every width

requirements.source: arith/exp2/rtl/exp2_lerp.sv (the product, sum and shift lines of the interpolation)
requirements.text: Within a segment of non-negative slope the interpolated value is non-decreasing in the position d, for every D, c0 and s. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation does not fall as the position grows, for every width

requirements.source: arith/exp2/rtl/exp2_cordic.sv (the x and y adders of one stage)
requirements.text: For every direction d = +-1 and every shift (scaled by u = 2^i), the step (u x + d y, u y + d x) multiplies x^2 - y^2 by exactly u^2 - 1, whatever the data: the hyperbolic gain is a data-independent constant. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: A hyperbolic CORDIC step scales x^2 - y^2 by a constant, for every width

requirements.text: For a packed pattern e * m + f with fraction f < m (m = 2^MAN), adding the rounding increment 1 either raises the fraction by one or, when the fraction is all ones, raises the exponent by one and leaves a zero fraction: the identity fp_pack's single add on the packed {exponent, fraction} pattern rests on, so a significand overflow, a subnormal rounding up to the smallest normal number and a largest finite number rounding up to infinity need no special case. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. requirements.text: For a value v with its leading one at bit k (2^k <= v < 2^(k+1)) and k < NW, shifting left by NW - 1 - k places gives a value in [2^(NW-1), 2^NW): the leading one is at bit NW - 1, which is what fp_norm's count lz = NW - 1 - msb does. designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function fp_fma (brief 139e). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/fp_fma/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (an enumeration of every finite value of a tiny format (the nearest one, ties to even), the multiplier and adder models, and the identities a * 1 + c = c + a and a * b + 0 = a * b) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (11 exhaustive points, 11 random ones, across 2 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (fused: STAGES; cascade: STAGES_M + STAGES_A), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/fp_fma/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_pack.sv (wsum: the increment added to the packed pattern)
requirements.text: For a packed pattern e * m + f with fraction f < m (m = 2^MAN), adding the rounding increment 1 either raises the fraction by one or, when the fraction is all ones, raises the exponent by one and leaves a zero fraction: the identity fp_pack's single add on the packed {exponent, fraction} pattern rests on, so a significand overflow, a subnormal rounding up to the smallest normal number and a largest finite number rounding up to infinity need no special case. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Rounding increment carries into the exponent, for every width

requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_norm.sv (the shift by the leading-zero count)
requirements.text: For a value v with its leading one at bit k (2^k <= v < 2^(k+1)) and k < NW, shifting left by NW - 1 - k places gives a value in [2^(NW-1), 2^NW): the leading one is at bit NW - 1, which is what fp_norm's count lz = NW - 1 - msb does. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Normalising left by NW - 1 - msb puts the leading one at the top, for every width

requirements.text: For a kept part hi and a discarded part lo below the threshold 2h, incrementing hi exactly when lo > h, or lo = h and hi is odd (the guard-and-sticky rule of fp_pack), gives a value within h of the exact one and, when it is exactly h away, even. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: The rounding decision is round-to-nearest, ties to even, for every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function multiplier (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/multiplier/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a shift-and-add formulation (and, for the Booth recoding, the digit-sum identity)) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: STAGES; lut_array: REG; booth_r4: REG), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/multiplier/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

designs.notes: Arithmetic library function sqrt_r4 (brief 139c). Every requirement is a draft written by the agent from the owner's request (spec_status: draft; only a human sets agreed). Evidence is generated by `python -m pytest arith/sqrt_r4/tests --junitxml=results/139c_arith/sqrt_r4_junit.xml` with ARITH_RECORD_DIR=results/139c_arith. The Lean items show 'statement not approved': lean_approvals.yaml is a human's. No Vivado run exists for this function (the build descriptions are prepared, not run), so there are no performance requirements.

requirements.text: For the radix-4 integer square root: the root and remainder equal math.isqrt for every radicand at W = 5 to 14 and for random values at W up to 200, are the same pairs and packing as arith/isqrt, and the radix-4 recurrence equals the root step by step with the register widths of the RTL asserted at every step (sh below 2**(QW+3), the three trial values below it, rem <= 2q).
requirements.title: The model is the specification: it equals integer arithmetic

requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of both variants against the model: every radicand at W = 5 to 16 (odd and even), with input gaps; root, remainder, order and latency checked.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, exhaustively at small widths

requirements.text: Simulation of both variants against the model with 3000 random and near-square values (remainders 0 and 2 * root) at W = 24, 31, 32, 48 and 64.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths

requirements.text: The measured latency equals the spec formula (RP + 1 and ceil(RP / PIPE), RP = ceil(RW / 2)) for PIPE = 1 to 5 at W = 13 (RP = 4) and PIPE = 3 and 4 at W = 24, one result per clock for the pipeline.
requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for either variant at W = 5, 6, 8, 13, 32 and 64 with PIPE = 1, 2 and 40.
requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean

requirements.text: Each of 18 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 18/18.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant satisfies root^2 + rem = x and rem <= 2 * root (so root^2 <= x < (root+1)^2) for all input sequences from reset: 11 jobs at W = 6 to 14; unbounded (abc pdr). 6 seeded faults are applied to the RTL and the same proof fails (bounded model checking finds the counterexample), which shows the harness is not vacuous.
requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent reference (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, no reference involved: sqrt_r4's pipeline and arith/isqrt's restoring pipeline (a different digit recurrence, written for the same specification, at its own latency, the shorter one delayed) give the same output on the same inputs, W = 8, 10, 12; unbounded (abc pdr): 3 jobs.
requirements.title: The radix-4 pipeline agrees with the radix-2 pipeline of arith/isqrt (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: The radix-4 digit recurrence of sqrt_r4_iter.sv and sqrt_r4_pipe.sv yields root and rem with root^2 + rem = x and rem <= 2 * root for every number of steps, which determines the floor square root. Proved in Lean, statement not approved; the Lean text is a transcription of the RTL's step, cross-checked against the Python model for every 8-bit radicand and every 17th 12-bit radicand; register widths are not modelled.
requirements.title: The radix-4 recurrence is a floor square root for every width (Lean)

requirements.text: For every variant of the radix-4 square root there is a build.yaml and an out-of-context clock constraint for xc7a100t and xck26, current against arith/tools/gen_build.py, consistent with the RTL (top, parameters, sources), with the expected primitive use evaluated for each point; the out-of-context wrapper lints clean and is functionally exact for the pipelined variant; the packaged verification harness (harness/run.py) passes on the library instance with every coverage bin hit. No Vivado run has been made: this requirement is about preparation, not about area, Fmax or power.
requirements.title: Out-of-context build descriptions are prepared for Artix-7 and K26 (not run)

requirements.text: Each order frame with a good FCS equals the reference frame byte for byte (Ethernet, IPv4, TCP headers, SoupBinTCP 3.00 length and type, OUCH 5.0 Enter Order fields, ClOrdID, appendage), the orders come in order with UserRefNum rising by one per accepted candidate, and a frame with a wrong FCS is never an order.
requirements.title: Every order that leaves with a good frame check sequence is byte exact

requirements.text: For every packet the packet, message, gap, missing, duplicate, overlap, session, heartbeat, end-of-session, short, truncated and bad-length counters and the gap, session-lock and end-of-session flags equal the reference model's at every checkpoint, with 1, 3 and 6 messages a packet and at every frame alignment.

requirements.text: Message-type counters, malformed and skipped messages, unwatched locates, missing/duplicate/overflowing orders, ladder overflow and over-execution counters, the candidate count and the per-instrument inexact flags equal the reference model's, including the edge cases of an empty book, a full ladder, a table-index collision and a replace.
requirements.title: The ITCH decoder and the book keep the counters, the inexact flags and the candidates the reference model computes

requirements.text: Not armed, kill switch, untrusted or gap-halted, inexact book, quantity, position limit per instrument, price band and missing bid refuse a candidate exactly as the reference does; the position and the order number advance only for an accepted candidate.
requirements.title: Every risk refusal is the first failing check, counted once, and no order starts on a refused candidate

requirements.text: Destination MAC (unicast or the group's multicast address), EtherType, IPv4 version and header length, fragments, protocol, destination address and port, UDP length against the IP length, and the IPv4 header checksum; EN = 0 drops everything.
requirements.title: Frames are forwarded or dropped by the first failing header check, and each drop is counted

requirements.text: With STRICT set (the default, owner decision 31) no order leaves with a good FCS when the frame that carried its message has a bad FCS, or when that frame's verdict is not yet known at the order's last word; such an order leaves with a wrong FCS. Cut-through is a documented option with a measured window.
requirements.title: Under STRICT an order is never sent on an unverified or bad frame

requirements.text: The TCP sequence number of an order is the loaded number plus 59 for every segment that left with a good FCS; a frame poisoned (wrong FCS) by the multiplexer, because its trigger frame was bad or unverified, does not advance it.
requirements.title: A poisoned order frame consumes no TCP sequence number

designs.notes: Simulation (cocotb on Icarus Verilog 12, one recorded pytest run) and out-of-context Vivado 2026.1 results only. No board run, no MAC of the 96 design in the simulation, no real TCP peer, no real exchange; every order is synthetic. Requirements that need those are hooks and show as not run.

requirements.text: For any connection state and order, the block sends 15 words (113 bytes without the frame check sequence) whose bytes equal the Python reference, with sequence number, acknowledgement number, window and IP identification captured at the go edge, the SoupBinTCP Unsequenced Data packet of brief 110 as payload, no TCP options and the PSH and ACK flags, including sequence numbers at the 32-bit wrap.
requirements.title: Each order leaves as one complete 113-byte Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP frame, byte exact against the reference

requirements.text: The IPv4 header checksum and the TCP checksum of every segment sent equal the reference's, which is itself checked against outside vectors (RFC 1071, a published IPv4 header), including carries in the fold, sums that wrap, a TCP checksum that comes out 0 and a segment whose headers sum to all ones. This is checked by simulation of chosen and random cases; the all-inputs statements are B119-F-CKSUM-IP, -TCP and -MODEL.
requirements.title: Both checksums on the wire are the RFC 1071 checksums, at the corner cases

requirements.text: One record (rec_v, rec_seq, rec_len, rec_id, rec_pay) for each unpoisoned segment in the clock of its last word, and none for a poisoned one, so software can retransmit from the records; a segment dropped on the wire is retransmitted by software with the same bytes.
requirements.title: Every segment that left is handed back to software, and none that was poisoned

requirements.text: Handshake, SoupBinTCP login, orders, acknowledgements, a dropped segment, heartbeats, a small window and a rejected login all behave as the software side documents, with the exchange seeing every order exactly once and in order.
requirements.title: A Python TCP owner and a software OUCH exchange run a whole session through the block

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall over tcp_fast.sv and the frame builder inside it reports no warnings, with the waivers in lint/lint_waivers.vlt.
requirements.title: The RTL lints clean

requirements.text: With tcp_fast in place of ouch_enter, brief 110's path against brief 110's reference model sends the same orders, with the same payload bytes, valid checksums and gapless sequence numbers; speculative orders that the risk logic refuses leave poisoned.
requirements.title: The block replaces the order port of brief 110 and works behind its risk logic

requirements.text: Writes to static fields invalidate the template and are ignored and counted while a segment is in flight; live fields are accepted at any time and restart the staleness age; reads show the registers before the next edge; unmapped addresses read 0; the 14 counters count what the datasheet says and clear on CLR_CNT.
requirements.title: The register bus and counters behave as the datasheet states

requirements.text: An abort at any of edges 1 to 14 ends the frame with o_poison, leaves SND_NXT and IP_ID as before and produces no record; an abort at edge 0 cancels the go; a speculative segment with no verdict by edge 14 is poisoned; an abort wins over a commit; an abort after the frame left is late, counted and ignored.
requirements.title: An aborted or unverdicted segment is poisoned and consumes no sequence space

requirements.text: Checked in the order busy, not armed, template not valid or state stale, window closed, MSS below 59, an order is refused with the matching code and counter, nothing leaves and no state changes; a window of exactly 59 bytes admits one segment and one byte less admits none.
requirements.title: The block refuses to send when it is not armed, stale, window-closed, too small or busy

requirements.text: Hardware and software share one sequence space. After a heartbeat takes it and gives it back, after an abort, after a refusal and after a retransmission, the peer's received stream has no gap and no duplicate, and nothing is sent by software while the block is armed and idle.
requirements.title: The peer sees no gap and no duplicate in the sequence space

requirements.text: The block sums the payload words ouch_enter actually emits and compares the total with the early one the checksum used; a difference (for example a configuration change in flight) poisons the segment and counts sumerr, so a wrong checksum is never sent as valid.
requirements.title: A segment whose payload disagrees with the checksum that was sent is poisoned

requirements.text: Every one of the seeded faults of verif/mutants.yaml that builds fails the bench (mutation score 100 percent, 73 of 73). The set is the agent's own; whether it is wide enough is the human's check.
requirements.title: A seeded fault anywhere in the checksum, segment, verdict, refusal or register logic is caught

requirements.external: the 96 design's MAC (mac64_tx) and, for the board, the KR260
requirements.text: tcp_fast and mac64_tx of designs/b96_kr260_10g simulated together. A 15-word segment is accepted without a pause, a short poisoned frame is padded as needed and its frame check sequence is wrong, and a good segment's is right. Not simulated yet.
requirements.title: The 96 design's MAC accepts the block's words every clock and corrupts the frame check sequence on o_poison

requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.
requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs

requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.
requirements.title: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words

requirements.text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.
requirements.title: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length

Unless a requirement says otherwise, "the default build" is RATE_MATCH = 0 (the board-proven 97C receive path) and "the rate-matched build" is rm_gp (RATE_MATCH = 1, RM_OWN = 1). Board evidence is one KR260 on a short optical loopback; nothing has run against a network card. Briefs 112 (UVM bench), 115 (formal proofs of the rate matcher) and 123 (pyuvm bench) are merged and their tests are in the recorded run; the bound SVA checkers in simulation and the coverage run have no evidence and are shown as not run.

requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.
requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model

requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.
requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions

requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.
requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors

requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.
requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart

requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.
requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path

requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.
requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame

requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)
requirements.text: For any constant receive clock offset from -300 to +300 ppm relative to the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. IEEE 802.3 allows +-100 ppm at each end, so two compliant ends differ by at most 200 ppm; +-300 ppm gives margin. A loopback has no offset, so a board test needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset

requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.
requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card

requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.
requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned

requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.
requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails

requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.
requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed

requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.
requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions

requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.
requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing

requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.
requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly

requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.
requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents

requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.
requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does

performance.condition: clock 6.206 ns, 100 link restarts, KR260 optical fibre loopback, fibre lead 0.17 m
performance.quantity: echo latency E (median of per-link minima)

requirements.text: Regression bound drawn from the 96E board record; the owner sets the target.
requirements.title: Echo latency E

performance.condition: clock 6.206 ns, 100 link restarts, KR260 optical fibre loopback, fibre lead 0.17 m
performance.quantity: trading-loop latency L (median of per-link minima)

requirements.text: Regression bound drawn from the 96E board record (L = 2E + D); the owner sets the target.
requirements.title: Trading-loop latency L

performance.condition: clock 6.206 ns, 100 link restarts, KR260 optical fibre loopback
performance.quantity: decision latency D (L - 2E from medians of minima)

requirements.text: D = L - 2E; the 96F1 pre-registration expects it unchanged within 1 clock of 12.
requirements.title: Decision latency D

performance.condition: xsim, RATE_MATCH = 1, RM_OWN = 1, clock phase 1550 ps
performance.quantity: tick-to-trade

requirements.text: Whole core in xsim with AMD's real XPM macros and the GT stand-in, own gray-pointer buffer; the GT, optics and clock-crossing phase are not in the simulation. Regression bound drawn from the 96E record.
requirements.title: Digital tick-to-trade, GT port to GT port

performance.condition: routed, Vivado 2026.1, user clocks 161.133 MHz and 100 MHz
performance.quantity: worst setup slack (WNS)

requirements.text: Every build closes timing on the 161.133 MHz and 100 MHz user clocks.
requirements.title: Post-route setup slack

performance.condition: routed, Vivado 2026.1
performance.quantity: worst hold slack (WHS)

requirements.text: Every build closes hold on all clocks.
requirements.title: Post-route hold slack

performance.condition: KR260 fibre loopback, one module, room temperature, eye-scan build
performance.quantity: eye width at BER 1e-9 (LPM equaliser)

requirements.text: Horizontal eye opening after the equaliser, read by the on-chip eye scan on the board. Draft bound for a short loopback; the owner sets the target.
requirements.title: Receive eye margin

performance.condition: build rm_gp_bypass, 100 receive restarts, KR260 optical fibre loopback, fibre lead 0.17 m
performance.quantity: echo latency E (median of per-link minima)

requirements.text: Build rm_gp_bypass must lower E by at least 1.5 clocks against rm_gp (21.0), else the bypass did not take effect. Pre-registered before any board time. Measured 2026-11-21 (stamp 86037ce1) as E = 17.0 clocks, 4.0 lower, inside the predicted 2.9 to 4.5 (results/b96f1/README.md).
requirements.title: GT buffer bypass shortens the echo path (pre-registered)

requirements.external: a 10G network card or a line-rate traffic generator

performance.condition: 1518-byte frames, 10 s burst, against a 10G network card
performance.quantity: frames lost in a line-rate burst

requirements.text: A burst at line rate loses no frame. Nothing has been measured; the line and payload rates stand on configuration and gearbox arithmetic only.
requirements.title: Line-rate throughput without loss

requirements.text: Build dbg_xvc (the eyescan build plus a PS-AXI Debug Bridge and one ILA) closes timing and report_cdc, adds no cell to and removes no cell from the core's hierarchy except the read-only taps, and, on the board, Vivado finds and captures from the ILA over XVC while Linux keeps running. Never part of a build whose latency is measured.
requirements.title: A debug build reaches an ILA over the network and leaves the trading path alone

requirements.text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.
requirements.title: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width

requirements.text: For every width and value, the decoder of the pointer crossing returns the count the encoder was given; and a sampled code that is the old or the new code decodes to the old or the new count.
requirements.title: Gray decoding inverts gray encoding, at every width

summary.line: 28 requirements (12 functional, 9 performance, 1 interface, 6 safety); 23 verified, of which 2 rest on delegated acceptances (the planner accepted the Lean statement on the owner's delegation; not human approvals); 1 stale; 2 failing; 2 with no passing evidence; 0 of 3 requirements that depend on an external element closed by hardware; performance verified: 5 on the board, 2 by post-route timing, 0 in simulation only; 0 of 28 requirements agreed by a human, 0 human review(s) recorded; 4 Lean proof item(s) (all widths): 0 with a human-approved statement, 4 with a statement accepted on the owner's delegation (not a human approval), 0 with statement not approved; 4 kernel only, 0 using a compiled decision procedure; build status from: recorded build (not re-run).

requirements.text: For the high-radix divider: quo and rem equal floor(a * 4**K / b) and a * 4**K - quo * b for every pair of normalised operands at W = 7 to 9 (K = 1, 3, 4), are the same pair as arith/divider (brief 139b) at width W + 2K, the selection table is what an exact-fraction search over every divisor interval and estimate cell finds, and the carry-save and carry-propagate SRT recurrences assert |u| <= 2b/3 after every step, the estimate error of 0 or 1 unit and the exactness of every step, for every pair at W = 7 and 8 (K = 1 to 4) and by random pairs to W = 64.
requirements.title: The model is the specification: it equals integer division, and the SRT recurrence converges

requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of all three variants against the model: every pair of normalised operands at W = 7 (K = 1, 3, 4), W = 8 (K = 2, 4, 5) and W = 9 (K = 4, 5), with input gaps; quotient, remainder, order and latency checked.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, exhaustively at small widths

requirements.text: Simulation of all three variants against the model with 3000 random and boundary-ratio pairs (ratios near 1/2, 2/3, 1, 4/3, 5/3, 2) at W = 12, 16, 24, 32 and 48 (K = 6 to 24).
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths

requirements.text: The measured latency equals the spec formula (K + 3 for the iterative variants, ceil((K + 1) / PIPE) + 1 for the pipeline) for PIPE = 1 to 7 at W = 8, K = 5, one result per clock for the pipeline.
requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for any variant at W = 7, 8, 16, 24, 32 and 64 (K = 1 to 32) with PIPE = 1, 3 and 40.
requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean

requirements.text: Each of 32 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 32/32. One more mutant (E02, the Q-1 register's initial value) and one (E01, the fix stage's sign bit) are equivalent by arguments given in verif/mutants.yaml and are not counted.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, the combinational step lemmas of formal/divider_hr_lemma_fv.sv for ALL inputs at a fixed width (6 widths, W = 7 to 16): L1 the first digit is 0, 1 or 2 and leaves |a - q*b| <= 2b/3; L2 the carry-save step, for ANY two words whose sum is bounded, sums to 4u - q*b and is bounded; L3 the same for the carry-propagate step; L4 the on-the-fly conversion keeps QM = Q - 1; L5 the fix returns the remainder in [0, b) and the right quotient. With the induction on the number of steps (proved in Lean for every K, DIVHR-F-LEAN-RECURRENCE) these are the correctness argument of the recurrence at that width.
requirements.title: The digit-recurrence step lemmas hold for all inputs (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: a * 4**K = quo * b + rem with 0 <= rem < b, for all input sequences from reset, unbounded (abc pdr) at W = 7, K = 1 for all three variants (3 jobs), bounded at W = 7, K = 3 (3 jobs; nothing claimed beyond the depth). The unbounded proof does not finish at K = 2 for the pipeline (400 s): the nonlinear relation between the quotient and remainder registers is not found by abc pdr; the lemmas above and the exhaustive simulation cover the larger K.
requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent characterisation (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, no reference involved: srt4_iter and srt4_cpa give the same in_ready, out_valid and out_data in every cycle: unbounded (abc pdr) at W = 7, K = 1 (1 job), bounded at W = 7, K = 3 (1 job).
requirements.title: The carry-save and carry-propagate iterative variants agree (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: For every number of digit steps K and every digit-selection rule that keeps the partial remainder bounded (|u| <= 2b/3, written 3|u| <= 2b), after K steps b * Q + U = 4**K * (b * q1 + u1) with U bounded, and the correction (Q - 1 and U + b when U < 0) is exactly floor(4**K * a / b) and 4**K * a mod b, with the remainder in [0, b). Proved in Lean, statements not approved; the digit-selection table's containment is NOT in Lean (it is an exact-fraction search in the model and the step lemmas above), and registers, widths, the carry-save form and the on-the-fly conversion are not modelled.
requirements.title: The SRT recurrence with any contained digit selection is a floor division for every K (Lean)

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function exp2 (brief 139d). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/exp2/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (exact rational (Fraction) evaluations of the interpolation and Horner formulas, a floating-point hyperbolic CORDIC, and the maths library's 2**x) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 12 random ones, across 4 variants), each variant's outputs equal its own model's (model.py, selected by variant) in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, table break points and random inputs at the large ones. The variants round differently and are not bit-identical to each other; the model of each is the bit-exact definition of that variant, and its distance from the exact function is the accuracy requirement.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against its own model

requirements.text: Each of the 12 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A point not listed has no stated bound.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is within the stated bound, at every listed point

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (table: REG; lerp: 2; poly2: 3; cordic: NIT + 1), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is bounded for all inputs, by proof, at a small input width

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/exp2/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.text: In a rising segment with break-point value c0 and slope s, the interpolated value (c0 * 2^D + s * d) / 2^D lies between c0 and c0 + s for every position d below 2^D and every D: the table variant cannot overshoot its segment. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation stays between the segment's end values, for every width

The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation does not fall as the position grows, for every width

requirements.text: For every direction d = +-1 and every shift (scaled by u = 2^i), the step (u x + d y, u y + d x) multiplies x^2 - y^2 by exactly u^2 - 1, whatever the data: the hyperbolic gain is a data-independent constant. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: A hyperbolic CORDIC step scales x^2 - y^2 by a constant, for every width

requirements.text: arith/fft/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (12 directed or exhaustive points, 8 random ones, across 2 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's: the directed points drive impulses at every position and tones at every bin (small N), DC, Nyquist, a chirp and corner values, forward and inverse, back to back and after the shortest legal gap; the random points drive random frames with random direction and legal gaps up to N = 4096. Each output frame equals the model bit for bit, the latency from in_sof to out_sof equals the formula, and out_valid is N consecutive clocks.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.title: The properties named in formal/jobs.yaml hold, by proof where the tools allow
