requirements.text: With out_ready driven low at random (40 per cent of the clocks) the burst variant's output frames equal the model bit for bit, and out_valid, out_sof and the data stay unchanged in every clock in which out_valid is high and out_ready low. The sdf variant ignores out_ready (stated).
requirements.title: The burst variant honours out_ready: stalling the sink changes nothing but the timing

requirements.text: For each variant, scaling mode and several N and twiddle widths, the error of the model (which the RTL equals bit for bit) against the double-precision FFT of NumPy is recorded in verif/results/accuracy.json: worst and rms error in units of the output LSB, and the SQNR and SFDR for a full-scale tone. The recorded worst error of the scaled mode is at most 6 LSB at every recorded point, and the unscaled mode's SQNR for noise-like input is at least 80 dB at every recorded point with twiddles of 16 bits or more (the unscaled word is W + LOGN bits wide, so its error in output LSBs is large for narrow twiddles: the SQNR is the figure to read); these are the bounds the test enforces, and the figures are what the report states, with no claim beyond them.
requirements.title: Accuracy against NumPy's FFT is measured and stated, per scaling mode

requirements.text: Through the RTL (both variants, the scaled mode), forward then inverse of the same frames returns the input divided by N (the scaled mode divides by N in both directions) to within 3 LSB, at the point of the round-trip test; the inverse is the swap of a forward transform, so forward and inverse results are related exactly by the swap.
requirements.title: A forward transform followed by an inverse transform returns the input within the stated error

requirements.text: arith/fft_common/fastconv.py (overlap-save and overlap-add on the bit-exact FFT models, both variants) equals numpy.convolve of the same samples and taps to within 8 LSB of the output word (N = 128 to 512, L = 1 to 65 taps, W = 16, TW = 18, WH = 24, FH = 14), the two methods agree with each other within the same bound, a unit filter passes the signal within 3 LSB, and a complex input is filtered part by part. This is a Python model and an interface proposal (docs/fft_suite_plan.md section 5), not RTL: the fast-convolution block is the next phase.
requirements.title: Fast convolution built on the FFT models equals direct convolution within the stated error (model only, phase 0)

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function fp_add (brief 139e). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/fp_add/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (an enumeration of every finite value of a tiny format (the nearest one, ties to even) and NumPy's hardware float32 addition) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 12 random ones, across 2 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (single_path: STAGES; dual_path: STAGES), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/fp_add/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_pack.sv (wsum: the increment added to the packed pattern)
requirements.text: For a packed pattern e * m + f with fraction f < m (m = 2^MAN), adding the rounding increment 1 either raises the fraction by one or, when the fraction is all ones, raises the exponent by one and leaves a zero fraction: the identity fp_pack's single add on the packed {exponent, fraction} pattern rests on, so a significand overflow, a subnormal rounding up to the smallest normal number and a largest finite number rounding up to infinity need no special case. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Rounding increment carries into the exponent, for every width

requirements.source: arith/fp_common/fp_norm.sv (the shift by the leading-zero count)
requirements.text: For a value v with its leading one at bit k (2^k <= v < 2^(k+1)) and k < NW, shifting left by NW - 1 - k places gives a value in [2^(NW-1), 2^NW): the leading one is at bit NW - 1, which is what fp_norm's count lz = NW - 1 - msb does. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Normalising left by NW - 1 - msb puts the leading one at the top, for every width

requirements.text: For a kept part hi and a discarded part lo below the threshold 2h, incrementing hi exactly when lo > h, or lo = h and hi is odd (the guard-and-sticky rule of fp_pack), gives a value within h of the exact one and, when it is exactly h away, even. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: The rounding decision is round-to-nearest, ties to even, for every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function log2 (brief 139d). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/log2/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (exact rational (Fraction) evaluations of the interpolation and Horner formulas, a floating-point hyperbolic CORDIC, and the maths library's log2) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 12 random ones, across 4 variants), each variant's outputs equal its own model's (model.py, selected by variant) in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, table break points and random inputs at the large ones. The variants round differently and are not bit-identical to each other; the model of each is the bit-exact definition of that variant, and its distance from the exact function is the accuracy requirement.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against its own model

requirements.text: Each of the 12 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A point not listed has no stated bound.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is within the stated bound, at every listed point

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (table: REG; lerp: 2; poly2: 3; cordic: NIT + 1), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is bounded for all inputs, by proof, at a small input width

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/log2/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.source: arith/log2/rtl/log2_lerp.sv (the product, sum and shift lines of the interpolation)
requirements.text: In a rising segment with break-point value c0 and slope s, the interpolated value (c0 * 2^D + s * d) / 2^D lies between c0 and c0 + s for every position d below 2^D and every D: the table variant cannot overshoot its segment. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation stays between the segment's end values, for every width

requirements.source: arith/log2/rtl/log2_lerp.sv (the product, sum and shift lines of the interpolation)
requirements.text: Within a segment of non-negative slope the interpolated value is non-decreasing in the position d, for every D, c0 and s. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation does not fall as the position grows, for every width

requirements.source: arith/log2/rtl/log2_cordic.sv (the x and y adders of one stage)
requirements.text: For every direction d = +-1 and every shift (scaled by u = 2^i), the step (u x + d y, u y + d x) multiplies x^2 - y^2 by exactly u^2 - 1, whatever the data: the hyperbolic gain is a data-independent constant. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: A hyperbolic CORDIC step scales x^2 - y^2 by a constant, for every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function mac (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/mac/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a structure-free reference that applies the samples one at a time with Python integers) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 12 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: NREG; dsp_cascade: LANES + 1; fabric: NREG), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/mac/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

designs.notes: Arithmetic library function recip (brief 139c). Every requirement is a draft written by the agent from the owner's request (spec_status: draft; only a human sets agreed). Evidence is generated by `python -m pytest arith/recip/tests --junitxml=results/139c_arith/recip_junit.xml` with ARITH_RECORD_DIR=results/139c_arith. No Vivado run exists for this function (the build descriptions are prepared, not run), so there are no performance requirements.

requirements.text: For the reciprocal: every variant's error (exact value minus result, in units of the last place, by exact rational arithmetic) is within the spec's bound over every normalised input at W = 8 to 12 for every A from 2 to W - 2, at W = 16 for A = 7 and 8, and over sampled inputs to W = 32; the Newton variants never exceed the exact value; the residual word never overflows its width (asserted at every step); the seed table entry is the nearest integer to the midpoint reciprocal.
requirements.title: The model is the specification: the error of every variant is within the stated bound

requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of all three variants against the model: every normalised b at W = 8 to 14 with several A (every A at W = 8 and 9), with input gaps; value, order and latency checked.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, for every input at small widths

requirements.text: Simulation of all three variants against the model with 3000 random and seed-table-boundary inputs at W = 16, 20, 24 and 32.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths

requirements.text: The measured latency equals the spec (1, 5 and 9 clocks for table, nr1, nr2), one result per clock, with back-to-back inputs at W = 10.
requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for any variant at W = 8, 10, 16, 24 and 32 (A = 3 to 10).
requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean

requirements.text: Each of 13 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 13/13. Two more mutants (E01, E02: the residual's reference value and shift type) are equivalent by arguments given in verif/mutants.yaml and are not counted.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant's result y satisfies the error characterisation (two products, no shared code with the RTL) for all input sequences from reset, proved by k-induction at an induction depth above the latency (the datapath is a feed-forward pipeline): 8 jobs (table, nr1, nr2 at W = 8, 10, 12). 7 faults or an over-tight bound make the proof fail (bounded model checking), which shows the harness is not vacuous. Not proved for other widths.
requirements.title: Every variant meets its error bound for all input sequences (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: For all integers S (the scale of 1.0), b and y: S*S - b*(y*(2S - b*y)) = (S - b*y)**2, hence b*y1 <= S*S: the exact Newton-Raphson reciprocal step squares the relative error and never exceeds the exact reciprocal. Proved in Lean, statements not approved; the truncations of the RTL (floor at every shift, two guard bits) and the seed table's accuracy are not in Lean (they are measured and proved at fixed widths by SymbiYosys).
requirements.title: The exact Newton reciprocal step squares the residual and never overshoots (Lean)

requirements.text: For every variant of the reciprocal there is a build.yaml and an out-of-context clock constraint for xc7a100t and xck26, current against arith/tools/gen_build.py, consistent with the RTL (top, parameters, sources), with the expected primitive use evaluated for each point; the out-of-context wrapper lints clean and is functionally exact for every variant; the packaged verification harness (harness/run.py) passes on the library instance with every coverage bin hit. No Vivado run has been made: this requirement is about preparation, not about area, Fmax or power.

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function sincos (brief 139d). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/sincos/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (an exact rational (Fraction) evaluation of the interpolation formula, a floating-point CORDIC, and the maths library's sin and cos) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 9 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal its own model's (model.py, selected by variant) in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, table break points and random inputs at the large ones. The variants round differently and are not bit-identical to each other; the model of each is the bit-exact definition of that variant, and its distance from the exact function is the accuracy requirement.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against its own model

requirements.text: Each of the 9 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A point not listed has no stated bound.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is within the stated bound, at every listed point

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (lerp: 2; poly2: 3; cordic: NIT), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is bounded for all inputs, by proof, at a small input width

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/sincos/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the bit-field split of the phase)
requirements.text: For every width k, a phase below 4 * 2^k splits into a quadrant (its top two bits) below 4 and an angle (the rest) so that quadrant * 2^k + angle is the phase again. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: The phase splits into a quadrant and an angle without loss, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the bit-field split of the phase)
requirements.text: For every width k, any quadrant and any angle below 2^k put together split back into the same quadrant and the same angle: the split is a bijection. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Every quadrant and angle pair is one phase, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the product, sum and shift lines of the interpolation)
requirements.text: In a rising segment with break-point value c0 and slope s, the interpolated value (c0 * 2^D + s * d) / 2^D lies between c0 and c0 + s for every position d below 2^D and every D: the table variant cannot overshoot its segment. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation stays between the segment's end values, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_cordic.sv (the x and y adders of one stage)
requirements.text: For every direction d = +-1 and every shift (scaled by u = 2^i), the step (u x - d y, u y + d x) multiplies x^2 + y^2 by exactly u^2 + 1, whatever the data: the CORDIC gain is a data-independent constant. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: A circular CORDIC step scales the squared length by a constant, for every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library function sqrt_r4 (brief 139c). Every requirement is a draft written by the agent from the owner's request (spec_status: draft; only a human sets agreed). Evidence is generated by `python -m pytest arith/sqrt_r4/tests --junitxml=results/139c_arith/sqrt_r4_junit.xml` with ARITH_RECORD_DIR=results/139c_arith. The Lean items show 'statement not approved': lean_approvals.yaml is a human's. No Vivado run exists for this function (the build descriptions are prepared, not run), so there are no performance requirements.

requirements.text: For the radix-4 integer square root: the root and remainder equal math.isqrt for every radicand at W = 5 to 14 and for random values at W up to 200, are the same pairs and packing as arith/isqrt, and the radix-4 recurrence equals the root step by step with the register widths of the RTL asserted at every step (sh below 2**(QW+3), the three trial values below it, rem <= 2q).
requirements.title: The model is the specification: it equals integer arithmetic

requirements.text: Simulation (Icarus 14) of both variants against the model: every radicand at W = 5 to 16 (odd and even), with input gaps; root, remainder, order and latency checked.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model, exhaustively at small widths

requirements.text: Simulation of both variants against the model with 3000 random and near-square values (remainders 0 and 2 * root) at W = 24, 31, 32, 48 and 64.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model at large widths

requirements.text: The measured latency equals the spec formula (RP + 1 and ceil(RP / PIPE), RP = ceil(RW / 2)) for PIPE = 1 to 5 at W = 13 (RP = 4) and PIPE = 3 and 4 at W = 24, one result per clock for the pipeline.
requirements.title: Latency and throughput are what the spec states

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall --lint-only reports nothing for either variant at W = 5, 6, 8, 13, 32 and 64 with PIPE = 1, 2 and 40.
requirements.title: The RTL is Verilator -Wall clean

requirements.text: Each of 18 seeded faults (one text change in the RTL, verif/mutants.yaml) makes the bench fail: killed/total = 18/18.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant satisfies root^2 + rem = x and rem <= 2 * root (so root^2 <= x < (root+1)^2) for all input sequences from reset: 11 jobs at W = 6 to 14; unbounded (abc pdr). 6 seeded faults are applied to the RTL and the same proof fails (bounded model checking finds the counterexample), which shows the harness is not vacuous.
requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent reference (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end, no reference involved: sqrt_r4's pipeline and arith/isqrt's restoring pipeline (a different digit recurrence, written for the same specification, at its own latency, the shorter one delayed) give the same output on the same inputs, W = 8, 10, 12; unbounded (abc pdr): 3 jobs.
requirements.title: The radix-4 pipeline agrees with the radix-2 pipeline of arith/isqrt (SymbiYosys)

requirements.text: The radix-4 digit recurrence of sqrt_r4_iter.sv and sqrt_r4_pipe.sv yields root and rem with root^2 + rem = x and rem <= 2 * root for every number of steps, which determines the floor square root. Proved in Lean, statement not approved; the Lean text is a transcription of the RTL's step, cross-checked against the Python model for every 8-bit radicand and every 17th 12-bit radicand; register widths are not modelled.
requirements.title: The radix-4 recurrence is a floor square root for every width (Lean)

requirements.text: For every variant of the radix-4 square root there is a build.yaml and an out-of-context clock constraint for xc7a100t and xck26, current against arith/tools/gen_build.py, consistent with the RTL (top, parameters, sources), with the expected primitive use evaluated for each point; the out-of-context wrapper lints clean and is functionally exact for the pipelined variant; the packaged verification harness (harness/run.py) passes on the library instance with every coverage bin hit. No Vivado run has been made: this requirement is about preparation, not about area, Fmax or power.
requirements.title: Out-of-context build descriptions are prepared for Artix-7 and K26 (not run)

content.framing: The human specifies the requirements and checks that the verification is thorough enough. The agent holds the knowledge to implement and to verify. You can open any of the implementation or the evidence, and you do not have to. Hardware on the board, with attached instruments, is a verification layer of its own: where a requirement depends on something outside the design (an optical link, a network card, a data source) it may be the only way to close it.
